summary: The bad() entry point reads a random int into `data` and uses it as an array index after only checking `data < array.length`. A negative random value passes this upper-bound check and causes an out-of-bounds read (CWE-129). Added a lower-bound check (`data >= 0`) so only valid indices index the array, while legitimate in-range values still work and the out-of-bounds branch still handles invalid indices.
